claim: Showing one concrete example to a human designer makes later ideas copy its features (Jansson-Smith effect); founding numbers still not read from the primary paper.
agent_test: Give agent a brief plus a flawed example vs none; count copied features at equal tokens.

claim: Telling people to avoid the example's flaws: Jansson-Smith (second-hand) reportedly still saw copying; Chrysikou and Weisberg 2005 (abstract read; N=89 and N=60) found defixating instructions DIMINISHED the fixation effect. Warnings are not reliably useless.
agent_test: Add an explicit avoid-X instruction in context and measure copying vs no instruction; also vs a warning that names the specific flawed feature.

claim: Replication is mixed: Perttula and Liikkanen (N=16, 8 per group) found no rise in example-feature reuse or idea count but fewer non-redundant categories (6.00 vs 13.00, p=.01); Purcell et al. 1993 reportedly saw fixation only when example matched domain familiarity (snippet only).
agent_test: Vary example count (1 vs 4 varied) and ideas per run; test whether fixation shows only early.

claim: Mental-set fixation is real and measurable in design: after 5 single-approach trials, 83% vs 44% used the costly approach on dual-approach trials (N=36), longer time (d=.70), more parts (d=.85); half the fixated group knew they were on autopilot.
agent_test: Run Luchins-style sequences; compare same-context vs fresh-context on the transfer trial.

claim: Meta-analysis of 43 design studies (Sio et al. 2015): examples narrow the range of ideas but raise novelty; quality rises with the degree of copying; facilitation is larger with fewer and less common examples; a single uncommon example helps most. Seen only in a search-result summary of the abstract; no effect sizes or moderator coefficients (gap 2 still open).
agent_test: Compare 1 rare example vs several common ones on novelty and category count.

claim: Debiasing by a lecture lowered fixation ratio 0.88 to 0.53 in 12 teams with no control group (p=.026).
agent_test: Weak; do not build on it.

claim: Within one session GPT-4o accumulates idea categories at the same rate as humans (slope 1.013 vs 1.035, p=.51): LLM within-session fixation is not worse than human.
agent_test: Replicate with Claude; slope of category accumulation over 10 sequential ideas.

claim: The LLM diversity gap is across sessions, not within: first ideas across LLM sessions overlap far more (pairwise distance 1.51 vs 2.41; first-idea categories 8.37 vs 14.51 per group of 10). Fresh contexts with an identical prompt do not give independent ideas. New: single-idea independent sessions were the least diverse arm (0.452 vs 0.679 for one session listing ideas, GPT-4o) and Claude Opus 4.8 sampled singly had distance 0.24 vs 0.80 for a set in one response.
agent_test: Sample N fresh contexts with identical prompt vs persona-diversified prompts; compare pairwise embedding distance at equal tokens.

claim: Seeding an LLM session with a human first idea does not raise later diversity (categories 18.34 vs 18.35).
agent_test: Seed a fresh context with a prior idea and check later-idea diversity.

claim: Chain-of-thought ideation (list 10 short titles, then revise bolder) cuts LLM fixation (slope 1.013 to 1.363; 1.095 in a robustness setup) and with ordinary personas gives 248 combinations vs human 197. It does not help humans. Persona+CoT category slope was not significant in the robustness check (p=.19).
agent_test: Plain list vs draft-then-revise-bolder at equal tokens; add everyday persona per fresh context.
audit_note: Single-paper result (Deng, Brucks and Toubia); the Meincke et al. listing only adds that CoT prompting raised GPT-4 diversity.

claim: Prompt strategy changes pool diversity: CoT best of 35 GPT-4 prompts (cosine 0.255 to 0.432 vs human 0.243); mixing strategies spreads more than repeating one.
agent_test: Mixed-prompt fresh contexts vs one prompt repeated, equal tokens.

claim: Same-model repetition is severe: average pairwise similarity exceeds 0.8 in 79% of cases; min-p at temperature 2.0 still has 61.2% of response pairs above 0.8; cross-model similarity ranges 71 to 82%. Temperature is a weak lever (Deng: temperature 1.5 gave only marginally more diversity, and 2.0 gave largely garbled text).
agent_test: Temperature vs prompt-level diversification vs verbalized sampling at equal tokens.
audit_note: Deng et al. report garbled text only at temperature 2.0; at 1.5 diversity rose only marginally (22 to 23 categories, 88 to 99 combinations), so '1.5 to 2.0 gave garbled text' is wrong.
claim_before_audit: Same-model repetition is severe: pairwise similarity above 0.8 in 79% of cases; min-p at temperature 2.0 still 61.2% above 0.8; cross-model similarity 71 to 82%. Temperature is a weak lever (Deng: temperature 1.5 to 2.0 gave garbled text).

claim: Over-generation saturates in one study: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 (5%) survive dedupe at cosine 0.8, even with earlier titles shown in the prompt. A second study (product ideas, pool of 100 to 1,000) saw coverage of the human idea space still improving with no plateau (mean nearest-neighbour distance 0.546 to 0.478). Saturation depends on task and measure.
agent_test: Track new non-duplicates per sample on our own task; stop spawning when a batch adds fewer than a set share of new items, and compare with a fixed count.

claim: Verbalized sampling (list several answers with probabilities) raises creative-writing diversity 1.6 to 2.1x and recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity, human raters agreeing.
agent_test: Test inside one context vs separate fresh contexts at equal tokens.

claim: In-context regeneration (show earlier answers, ask for different) lifts Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro to roughly human-level NoveltyBench diversity; listing a set in one response beats independent single samples for Claude Opus 4.8 (distance 0.80 vs 0.24). Separate point, one source: more reasoning effort gave fewer distinct generations for the OpenAI o-series and no change for Gemini 2.5 Flash.
agent_test: Show-previous regeneration vs independent fresh samples at equal tokens.
audit_note: Evidence labels attribute NoveltyBench to Jiang et al. in some lines and Zhang et al. in others; the claim itself names no author.

claim: AI image help raises human fixation on a researcher's example (+.32 log-link coefficient, BF 124, N=60; image search +.27) and shifts fixation to the AI's latest images.
agent_test: Show the agent its own earlier outputs vs none and score feature reuse.

claim: Exposure to AI ideas raises rated novelty (+5.4%, +8.1%) but raises similarity to the AI idea (+5.2%) and across stories; benefit largest for low-creativity writers.
agent_test: Does cross-context idea sharing help weak runs more than strong runs.

claim: Group-level homogenisation from LLM assistance appears even when individual diversity is unchanged; it comes from shared suggestions. Feedback-tuned InstructGPT homogenises; base GPT-3 does not.
agent_test: Judge across-run diversity, not within-run; compare base-like vs aligned model.
audit_note: Anderson et al. is a small within-subject study (N=36); Padmakumar and He used 38 writers; the group-level effect is not shown for the base model in Anderson.

claim: Post-training lowers diversity and creates attractor states (Llama-2 chat vs base; Tulu SFT/DPO/RLVR stages).
agent_test: Check cross-sample variance of our model with and without persona prompt.
audit_note: Minor: the 182.6% Tulu figure is measured after the DPO stage for the poem task, not at a final RLVR stage; Mohammadi gives no numeric entropy in abstract but text says base entropy significantly higher.

claim: LLMs show anchoring: a number or hint in the prompt pulls answers and chain-of-thought and reflection did not remove it (Lou and Sun 2024); in multi-turn chat models average 35 to 39% lower performance than with the full task at once, partly because they make early assumptions, attempt answers prematurely and overly rely on them (Laban 2025); restating all information in a final turn (recap) or each turn (snowball) recovers some but not all of the loss.
agent_test: Multi-turn refinement vs fresh restart with summary at equal tokens.
audit_note: Laban's 35-39% is the total average drop from single-turn to sharded multi-turn (aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%), not a cost isolated to early guesses; early premature answers are only one identified cause.
claim_before_audit: LLMs show anchoring and early-commitment effects: prompted numbers pull answers (CoT and reflection did not remove it); multi-turn early guesses cost 35 to 39%; recap recovers some.

claim: Independent sampling with a verifier raises coverage log-linearly (15.9% to 56% from 1 to 250 samples); without a verifier gains plateau. At matched budget with a verifier, sequential revisions narrowly beat parallel on MATH overall, while hard items need a mix. Dropping low-confidence terminations before voting added 2.6 to 4.9 points in long-horizon search.
agent_test: Many fresh contexts plus a checker vs one long context.
audit_note: Minor: Xia et al. call the dropped terminations give-up or uncertain-answer endings (not 'low-confidence'), and report the gain as 2.6% to 4.9% across aggregation rules.

claim: Population variability of 22 LLMs is far below 102 humans (AUT cosine 0.459 vs 0.738) while mean originality is comparable; system prompt changes do not fix it.
agent_test: Persona diversification across contexts is the lever, not a creative system prompt.
audit_note: Minor: the 22 LLMs' mean originality was slightly higher than humans (0.711 vs 0.695 on AUT) rather than identical; 'comparable' is fair.

claim: Design fixation as a property of GenAI is proposed qualitatively; 7 of 10 noticed ChatGPT repetition. Evidence thin.
agent_test: Treat as hypothesis only.

claim: Strategy cards for idea generation had no fixation control and do not test fixation.
agent_test: Exclude from fixation evidence.

claim: Many bare single-idea fresh contexts with the same prompt are worse for diversity than one context that writes a list: GPT-4o 0.452 vs 0.679 (1 minus pairwise cosine); Claude Opus 4.8 distance 0.24 vs 0.80. The list costs per-idea quality (win rate 0.33 to 0.21), so utility moved little.
agent_test: Compare N fresh single-idea contexts vs one list of N per context at equal tokens, scoring both diversity and best-idea quality.
audit_note: Minor: Terwiesch table lists the CoT arm and independent-session arm separately; the Opus 0.24 vs 0.80 and 0.33 vs 0.21 values come from Wadhwa Table 12/11 on scientific ideas, not product ideas.

claim: Random personas or constraints injected per session restore most ideation diversity (random persona 0.757, constraints 0.735, humans 0.773; GPT-4o product ideas), and curated personas lifted a judged score in an industry paper (+4.76; first persona version not significant). Over-eccentric personas add nothing.
agent_test: Per fresh context, assign a short persona or constraint; compare pairwise distance with an identical-prompt arm.

claim: On correctness tasks expert personas cost accuracy and temperature spread does nothing: MMLU 71.6% to 68.0% with an expert persona (Hu et al. 2026); maximally diverse persona teams lost 2.1 to 4.4 points on CSQA versus plain debate and temperature spread changed accuracy by only -0.11 to -0.41 points (Ferreira et al. 2026, small open models). Separately, Wu et al. argue that splitting a sampling budget across distinct reasoning modes beats sampling from one mixed distribution (0.5B-7B models). No Claude model was tested.
agent_test: On proofs or code, compare plain independent samples vs strategy-prefix samples (induction, contradiction, brute force) with a verifier at equal tokens.
audit_note: The numbers match (Hu 71.6 to 68.0; Ferreira CSQA -2.1 to -4.4 and temperature spread -0.11 to -0.41pp), but 'diversity helps only as strategy-mode coverage' is not shown by any source: Wu et al. show mode-conditioning helps pass@k on math in 0.5B-7B models, not that nothing else helps.
claim_before_audit: On correctness tasks personas cost accuracy and temperature spread does nothing: MMLU 71.6% to 68.0% (expert persona); CSQA -2.1 to -4.4 points with diverse persona teams; temperature spread -0.11 to -0.41. Diversity helps only as strategy-mode coverage (mode-conditioning argument). No Claude test.

claim: Repeated refinement of the model's own ideas lowers set diversity (make-it-bolder twice: 0.575 vs 0.679 plain), a local-search trap; showing earlier titles slowed but did not stop duplication (Si et al.).
agent_test: Compare iterative refinement of one context against fresh restarts from the same seed at equal tokens.

claim: Agents repeat the same blocked mechanism (mechanism shift failure) on every model tested; a threshold-triggered divergent-then-select switch raised Claude Sonnet 4.6 path discovery from 53.6% to 73.2% (GPT-5.4 48.2% to 67.9%), while generic Self-Refine lowered Claude to 44.6%. Share of agent errors due to mental set is not reported.
agent_test: Count repeated same-mechanism failures per target; trigger a switch when it passes a threshold; compare with generic self-critique.

claim: Summarising or trimming context in long agent runs raises accuracy by cutting premature stopping: a length-triggered summary at 32K gave 57.7% vs 41.7% at 64K (Qwen3.5-397B, BrowseComp), inconclusive failures 2.4% vs 20.2%. The best method depends on model strength. Closed models untested.
agent_test: Vary the summary-trigger length for our agent; log give-up and uncertain-answer terminations.

claim: Human incubation: exposure to others' ideas did not hurt in the first 10 minutes but did in the last 10 minutes (exposed-immediate produced 2.48 and 1.75 fewer ideas than exposed-relax and exposed-task in the last 10 min; over the full 20 min -3.21, p=.003 and -2.38, p=.029); a relax or unrelated-task break removed the deficit. Meta-analysis (Sio and Ormerod 2009): positive incubation effect, divergent tasks gain more than insight tasks, longer preparation gives a larger effect, high-demand filler tasks give a smaller effect. The agent analogue (context truncation or reset) is untested for fixation.
agent_test: Run ideation, then reset context keeping only a summary of rejected directions, and measure new-category yield after the reset.
audit_note: Zhou et al. 2019 Table 3 values -3.21 (p=.003) and -2.38 (p=.029) are for ideas in the total 20 minutes, not the late window; last-10-min differences are -2.48 (p<.001) and -1.75 (p=.010); also Sio and Ormerod say high-demand filler gives a smaller incubation effect, not that it hurts.
claim_before_audit: Human incubation: exposure to others' ideas hurts mostly late, not in the first 10 minutes; relax or unrelated-task breaks remove the deficit (idea count -3.21, p=.003; -2.38, p=.029). Meta-analysis: divergent tasks gain most from incubation, long preparation helps, high-demand filler hurts. The agent analogue (context truncation or reset) is untested for fixation.

claim: Current Claude with reasoning reaches physician-level performance on the mARC Einstellung benchmark: Claude 4.1 Opus 0.751 vs physicians 0.66 (difference not significant); on the 20 items most physicians missed it was decisively correct on 55.0%, decisively wrong on 25.0% and indeterminate on 20.0%. Earlier models failed (o1 48% on mARC; GPT-4 solved only 3 to 7 of 494 red-herring walls vs 285 for humans).
agent_test: Use a mental-set probe (misleading cue plus a flexible-override item) to gate whether restart operators are worth their cost for the current model.
audit_note: Shidara et al. report Claude 4.1 Opus (0.751) is not significantly different from physicians (0.66, CI 0.55-0.75) and wrong or indeterminate on 45% of the human-miss items; 'largely avoids' overstates 'human-level'. Minor: GPT-4 solved 3 to 7 walls depending on shots (6 at 0-shot).
claim_before_audit: Current Claude with reasoning largely avoids an Einstellung trap benchmark: Claude 4.1 Opus 0.751 vs physicians 0.66 on mARC; on the 20 items physicians missed it was decisively correct on 55.0%. Earlier models failed (o1 48%; GPT-4 solved 6 of 494 red-herring walls vs 285 human).

claim: Gap status: exact Jansson-Smith 1991 numbers and Sio 2015 effect sizes remain unread; no in-context flawed-example replication in LLMs and no test of delayed vs up-front example exposure in agents was found; no Claude extended-thinking anchoring test was found.
agent_test: Build the missing tests in our own harness instead of citing literature.
